stories.title: Iran blames US as fears of new strikes grow
stories.body: President Masoud Pezeshkian blamed Washington for the collapse of an interim deal to end the war and said both sides should return to it. President Trump said he "may do another little Epic Fury", the codename of the US–Israeli campaign that began on 28 February. The Revolutionary Guards warned that even limited strikes would bring a response several times greater. Iran's Supreme Leader is now Mojtaba Khamenei, who succeeded his father and has not been seen in public since early March.
stories.why: A return to full-scale strikes would push oil and shipping costs even higher for Nigeria.

cards.front: What is the codename of the US–Israeli war on Iran that began on 28 February 2026?

stories.title: Former DSS chief Bichi to chair the National Institute for Security Studies
stories.body: President Tinubu approved Yusuf Magaji Bichi, the immediate past Director-General of the DSS, as chairman of the Governing Board of the National Institute for Security Studies (NISS) in Abuja. He serves an initial four-year term from 22 October 2026 and succeeds A.A. Gadzama. The appointment was recommended by the current DSS Director-General, Oluwatosin Ajayi.
stories.why: NISS trains officers across Nigeria's security and intelligence community, so its leadership is a fair general-knowledge question.

cards.front: Who chairs the Governing Board of the National Institute for Security Studies (as of October 2026)?
cards.back: Yusuf Magaji Bichi, former Director-General of the DSS.

stories.title: Gunmen attack opposition candidate's convoy in Ebonyi
stories.body: Gunmen attacked the convoy of Rollins Offia-Nwali, the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) candidate for the Ezza South seat in the Ebonyi State House of Assembly, on 22 October. Police said one person died and three were wounded, and the candidate's vehicle was set on fire. The attack came days after the President ordered security agencies to protect voters and candidates ahead of the 2027 elections.
stories.why: Election violence is a growing risk as 2027 approaches, especially in the South-east.

stories.title: Putin agrees to resume US-brokered talks on Ukraine
stories.body: US envoy Steve Witkoff met President Putin in Saint Petersburg, with Jared Kushner joining online. Putin agreed to resume US-mediated peace talks with Ukraine, the first since February 2026. The envoys proposed a three-way technical meeting on post-war security guarantees, which Ukraine had accepted in Oslo the day before. The Kremlin says talks could be held in Abu Dhabi from November. Russia also freed American Stephen Hubbard, 74.
stories.why: A path back to talks matters for world food and fuel prices that affect Nigeria.

cards.front: Where did Putin meet US envoy Witkoff on 21 October 2026, and what did he agree?
cards.back: Saint Petersburg; to resume US-mediated peace talks with Ukraine, possibly in Abu Dhabi from November.

stories.title: Qatar: the energy shock from the Iran war has not peaked
stories.body: Qatar's defence minister, Sheikh Saoud bin Abdulrahman Al Thani, told the Global Security Forum in Doha that the world has not yet felt the worst of the war's effect on energy. Iranian strikes in March damaged Qatar's Ras Laffan gas complex, and repairs will take several years. He rejected any transit fees for ships in the Strait of Hormuz. Qatar, Pakistan and Oman are mediating between the US and Iran.
stories.why: Qatar is one of the world's biggest gas exporters, so damage there keeps global energy prices high for importers and raises the value of Nigeria's own gas.

cards.front: Which Qatari gas complex was damaged by Iranian strikes in March 2026?
cards.back: Ras Laffan; repairs are expected to take several years.

stories.title: AES and ECOWAS hold first talks since the split
stories.body: Ministers from ECOWAS and the Alliance of Sahel States (Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger) met in Dakar, Senegal, on 17 October. ECOWAS was led by Senegal's Foreign Minister Cheikh Niang and the AES by Burkina Faso's Foreign Minister Karamoko Jean-Marie Traoré. They agreed to set up joint working groups to draft a cooperation framework based on good neighbourliness and respect for sovereignty. The talks are about cooperation, not about the three states rejoining, and no timeline or trade deal was announced.
stories.why: Nigeria shares a long border with Niger, so any security and trade cooperation with the AES directly affects the North-west and North-east.

cards.front: Where did ECOWAS and the AES hold ministerial talks in October 2026?
What did ECOWAS and the AES agree in Dakar in October 2026?
cards.back: To set up joint working groups to draft a cooperation framework. Rejoining ECOWAS was not agreed.
